in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you find out if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To get started, could you please tell me how many children you're looking to claim Child Benefit for, and what are their names and ages?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! I'm looking to claim Child Benefit for my child Alex, who is 8 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information about Alex.

To assess your eligibility, I have a few questions:

Are you responsible for Alex's care? This means Alex lives with you, or you contribute at least the same amount as Child Benefit towards their upkeep.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, Alex lives with me at home. I'm responsible for their care.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
That's great, thank you for confirming.

Next question: Do you live in the UK? And if so, are you a UK citizen, or do you have settled or pre-settled status, or another form of immigration status that allows you to claim benefits?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK - I'm in Birmingham. And yes, I'm a UK citizen.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Lovely, thank you for confirming that.

Just a couple more questions:

Is Alex in full-time education, and are they your biological child, stepchild, or adopted child, or do you care for them in another capacity (such as being a foster parent or other guardian)?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Alex is my biological child. They're 8, so yes, they're in primary school - full-time education.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information.

One last question: Is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex, or has anyone else applied to claim Child Benefit for them?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Thank you for providing all that information. Based on what you've told me, I have everything I need to assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great news! Based on the information you've provided, **you appear to be eligible for Child Benefit for Alex**. Here's a summary:

**For Alex (age 8):** ✅ Eligible

- Alex is under 16 years old
- You are Alex's biological parent and responsible for their care
- Alex lives with you
- You are a UK citizen living in the UK
- No one else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex

**Next steps:**
You can apply for Child Benefit online or by post. You'll need your National Insurance number, Alex's birth certificate (or adoption certificate), and your bank or building society details.

Please note that if you or your partner earn over £60,000 a year, you may have to pay back some or all of the Child Benefit as a tax charge (known as the High Income Child Benefit Charge). However, it may still be worth claiming even in this situation, as it helps protect your National Insurance record.

Is there anything else you'd like to know about Child Benefit?
